label: prop:beta-stability
title: Beta-stability line from the Skein binding Lagrangian
html:
The stable neutron number n^*(p) for each element is determined by extremizing the Skein binding Lagrangian over n at fixed p.

Scope of the liquid-drop coefficient identification. The coefficient assignments a_C = (q - q^{-1})[6]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}} and a_A = 3[2]_q[7]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}} are not derived in the corpus; they are assigned. The functional form A/(2 + a_C A^{2/3}/(2a_A)) is the liquid-drop (SEMF) beta-stability line, imported from the literature rather than derived from the Skein binding Lagrangian. Read this block as a conjectural identification, not as a proved proposition.

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q. For a multi-nucleon Hopf link L = Z\mathfrak{p} \oplus N\mathfrak{n} with A = Z + N, the beta-stable configuration satisfies \partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} / \partial n = 0. This gives the beta-stability line:

  p^*(A)
  = 
  \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)}

where a_C is the Coulomb coefficient from the crossing asymmetry and a_A the Pauli asymmetry coefficient. Both are fixed by the q-integer coefficient assignments of the seven-term mass formula:

  a_C \;=\; \lambda_C \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\,[6]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}},
  \qquad
  a_A \;=\; a_{\mathrm{asym}} \;=\; 3\,[2]_q\,[7]_q\,\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{e}} .

The factor (q - q^{-1}) belongs to \lambda_C and appears once: writing a_C = (q - q^{-1})\cdot\lambda_C would apply it twice.

Equivalently, for a given p, the stable mass number is the fixed point of:

  A^*(p) = p \left(2 + \frac{a_C}{2a_A} {A^*}^{2/3}\right)

and n^*(p) = A^*(p) - p.
